quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: The indemnity package meets the preferred position in full. Section 20.1 gives an uncapped-in-scope Vendor IP defence and indemnity covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel for claims that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP, with no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions cut into the grant. Section 20.2 adds Vendor indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud — matching (b)-(d) of our model language. Section 20.4 is a balanced, reciprocal procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, control of defence, delay excusing only to the extent of material prejudice, and no adverse settlement without consent). Section 20.5 provides the infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace without materially reducing functionality, or terminate and refund on a straight-line three-year basis), with Vendor barred from terminating unaffected Services, and is reinforced by the termination right in Section 9.3. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in Section 20.3 is appropriately narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with express carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. Section 21.3 treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, so Vendor's indemnities sit outside the liability cap; this is better than the fallback's 3× super-cap and requires no change. No redline proposed.

The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event and (b) USD 1,000,000; § 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually (and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages); and § 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to place confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP outside both the cap and the damages exclusion. § 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" and § 21.4 preserves liabilities that cannot lawfully be limited. "Fees" (§ 1.5) is a meaningful base covering subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory; the only minor gap is that Fees exclude a one-time implementation charge, which we note but do not redline. No competing or one-sided liability language appears elsewhere (§ 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). The § 7.6 liquidated-damages and indemnity points are addressed under their own rules and are not double-flagged here.

rationale: Section 8.2 auto-renews each Order Form for twelve months (acceptable term length) but conditions non-renewal on 180 days' advance notice. That exceeds both the preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day opt-out windows and falls into walk-away territory (windows longer than 90 days). We therefore shortened the window to 30 days, matching the preferred position and approved precedent. Pricing is not an issue: § 8.3 caps renewal uplifts at the lesser of CPI and 3%, requires 90 days' notice, and exempts prepaid periods, which meets the preferred cap and is favourable to us. The absence of a Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before renewal is a minor gap from the preferred wording only and is noted rather than flagged.

quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
rationale: Section 9 provides only cause-based rights: material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and Customer's special termination triggers (9.3), plus a force-majeure exit in 27.3 and refund/warranty exits in 6.2, 19.4 and 20.5. A full-text search returns no termination-for-convenience right anywhere, and no 9.4 exists. Because the Agreement runs for three years (8.1) and Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months (8.2), the absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule, so it fails the fallback. There is no Vendor convenience right, which is favourable to us; our redline inserts a new 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (consistent with the refund mechanic already in 10.2) and confirms Vendor has none.
